title: Meals Every Firefighter Knows
subtitle: The short list — chili, burgers, tacos, pasta
description: Meals every firefighter knows from station kitchens: chili, burgers, tacos, pasta bakes, and BBQ — the shared vocabulary of hall food.
intro: You can walk into most halls and predict three dinners from the freezer and whiteboard. Chili, burgers, tacos, pasta bake, BBQ chicken — these are not clichés. They are the shared language of crews who cook under interruption. Below: what halls actually cook for meals firefighters know — formats, timing, and recipe picks that survive a busy board.

sections.heading: The hall canon
paragraphs: Chili, smash burgers, taco bar, chicken parm, pulled pork, mac and cheese, sheet-pan fajitas. If you can cook these, you can feed most crews.
On shift, write the hold plan on the whiteboard — covered on low, finish sear when you're back — so the next cook is not guessing at your flat-top settings.
tips: Assign one cook and one runner; keep everyone else out of the kitchen until called.
Label allergens on the line once — it stops the mid-meal Q&A loop.

sections.heading: Why the canon works
paragraphs: These meals scale, survive holds, and need no fine dining timing. They are what crews suggest when someone asks 'what should we make?'

sections.heading: What this looks like on the hall tonight
paragraphs: Kitchen culture shows up in small moves: who shops, who cleans, whether rookies get coached or roasted. For meals firefighters know, fairness beats perfection — rotate the jobs that nobody wants twice in a row.
Meals are morale. A crew that trusts the kitchen cooks more often and complains less about grocery splits. Keep the tone direct and the help real.
tips: Praise the cook in the bay — fix critiques one-on-one after cleanup.
Write grocery splits on the receipt photo the same night you shop.

practicalAdvice: Master one meal in each category — your hall will thank you.
Teach rookies one batch meal and one line meal.
Keep the shopping list for your hall canon posted — repetition builds speed.
Post who's cooking and what's holding warm on the whiteboard — post-call eaters should not hunt for answers.
